skill.name: Understand Iterator Data Sink for Testing
skill.description: Reference skill for understanding iterator-based data sinks in DataStream testing. Documents the collectAsync() sink pattern for collecting and inspecting DataStream results in test and debugging scenarios.
skill.skill_body:
Use this reference to understand iterator data sink patterns in DataStream testing. Review the collectAsync() method for collecting results and appropriate use cases for test assertions and debugging inspection.

## Objective

provide testing patterns for iterator-based result collection
## Applicable Signals

- collecting DataStream results for validation
- inspecting results in test assertions
- debugging DataStream output

## Contraindications

- runtime execution in production environments
- production deployment scenarios
- high-volume result collection

## Constraints

- Iterator sink (collectAsync) is for testing and debugging only
- Not intended for production result collection

## Cautions

- Do not use iterator sink for production result collection
- Be aware this is a testing-only pattern

## Output Contract

- Iterator of collected DataStream results suitable for test assertions and debugging inspection

## Example Executions

### Example 1

- Input: Need to collect and inspect DataStream results for validation
- Output: Use myResult.collectAsync() to retrieve Iterator of results
- Notes: Intended for test assertions and debugging inspection only
